fun_highlights: The four-vocation calling card (y_calling) is a genuine structural fork — a soldier's life actually produces different adult cards than a scholar's, with era-vocation intersections (vx_soldier_war, vx_scholar_turning, vx_maker_plenty) landing as a real surprise when they fire.

Callback cards are the game's single best mechanic: cb_outcast_return (a childhood kindness returned decades later), cb_study_pays (the scholar's hungry bet cashing in), cb_lookaway (facing a second chance to help after looking away young) create genuine 'oh, that' recognition moments that feel earned.

Era cards (plague, war, plenty, turning, hard) meaningfully reframe cards that would otherwise be generic — the y_calling text in a war era is a different card than in settled times, and this is visible in the transcripts with Elias Okonkwo's war-era road choice.

The dynasty house layer — seat climbs, reputation drift, motto crystallization, heirlooms, secrets, bequest — gives each new life a concrete starting situation and something specific to chase. Watching 'We burn bright, and we burn' crystallize across the Vasquez line (D4) is genuinely satisfying.

Solitary and childless life-shapes are properly supported with their own card arcs (m_solitary, a_chosen_family, e_solitary, e_childless), and Niall Vasquez (D7) plays as a meaningfully different shape of life.
Early death (Felix Okafor, 21 years; Yara Reyes, 43 years) is handled with grace and lands as a real gut punch rather than a mechanical failure state.
The fate cards (f_fire, f_sudden_loss, f_grace, f_reversal) with no choice — just an outcome — are a smart design beat that breaks the player's sense of total agency and makes the world feel real.
staleness: The 'red and furious and entirely unimpressed by any of it' first-child line appears verbatim in Dynasties 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, and 15 across the 15-dynasty transcript. The _usedFurious guard resets per dynasty, so every dynasty's first child after a chance(0.4) roll lands this same phrase. By dynasty 6 it reads as a running joke, not a fresh moment.

The love card (y_love1) has 7 prose variants that rotate among all the lives that fall in love young, and 'Meet them halfway' is accepted in nearly every instance. By dynasty 6 the love-beat is utterly predictable: someone appears at the edges of the days, the player clicks the first choice, a name is generated. The beat has lost all surprise.
The t_guarded trait card fires in Dynasties 1, 3, 7, and 15 with word-for-word identical prompt text and 'Keep the wall' chosen repeatedly. It reads as a stamp, not a character moment.

'Burned the old letters without reading them, and let the younger self she'd been keep, at last, her privacy' appears verbatim in Dynasties 6, 7, 8 (twice), and 13 — five times in 15 dynasties, across unrelated characters. The e_old_letters card fires too frequently and the 'burn unread' option dominates, so the same outcome line repeats without variation.

The s_from_nothing card ('no name that means a thing, no floor to fall back to') fires in nearly every early-dynasty adult life regardless of actual house standing — it appears at age 27 for Cosima (D1), 36 for Cyrus Marchetti (D2, after already having a child and a maker's career), 50 for Vesna (D3), 27 for Hale (D6-3). The cond (seat<=1) is either too loose or the card misfires, but the effect is that a 'starting from nothing' framing keeps landing on lives that clearly aren't.

Epitaph recycling becomes visible by dynasty 8: 'Gave away everything she knew, and so kept it' vs 'Gave away everything he knew, and so kept it' hit in D1, D6, D7, D9 — the teacher-cluster epitaphs exhaust themselves because teaching is a common life outcome. The code has anti-repeat logic but the pool is too small relative to how often the 'became_teacher' cluster is reached.

The adult structural cadence — love, child, work-promotion, aging parent, midlife health scare, elder legacy — is felt by dynasty 5-6 as a skeleton the cards are hung on rather than emergent story. Individual card text varies, but the sequence shape is recognizable enough that a player can anticipate what decade-of-life card is coming next.

The cb_outcast_return callback (childhood friend who became somebody) fires in five of the fifteen dynasties and becomes predictable as a mechanic: make friend in yard -> expect payoff in adulthood. The surprise of the first instance becomes a formulaic beat by the third.

The a_child log lines for the first child rotate well within a dynasty but across dynasties the 'red and furious' anchor and 'some door hadn't known was shut came quietly open' recur across unrelated houses, flattening what should feel like distinct births.

improvements.what: Make the _usedFurious flag session-global (attach to a module-level RECENT_LINES-style set) rather than per-dynasty (S._usedFurious). Expand the first-child log pool by 6-8 lines so no single phrase can appear more than once per session of play.
improvements.why: 'Red and furious and entirely unimpressed by any of it' appears 11+ times across 15 dynasties in the transcript — the single most visible verbatim repeat. It undercuts every birth after the first.

improvements.what: Add 4-6 additional prose variants to y_love1 (currently 7) and weight the 'Pretend not to notice' choice so it fires 25-30% of the time via the engine's nudge rather than being nearly always bypassed, producing more lives that miss early love and need the late or solitary arc.
improvements.why: In the transcript, love is accepted in approximately 90% of eligible youth lives via 'Meet them halfway'. The beat is mechanically inevitable, which means it stops feeling like a choice and the prose variants (all framing someone appearing at the edges of the days) become wallpaper.

improvements.what: Add a session-level seen-recently guard to e_old_letters and t_guarded (similar to RECENT_LINES for epitaphs) so each fires at most once per 4-5 lives across the whole session, not just per dynasty.
improvements.why: These two cards have no onceDyn gate and shallow enough pools that they repeat verbatim within a single evening's play. e_old_letters fires in 5 of 15 dynasties; t_guarded fires in 4 of 15 with identical prompt text each time.

improvements.what: Tighten the s_from_nothing cond to require seat<=0 (not seat<=1) OR add an age/life-progress gate so it only fires before the player has accumulated a visible career, marriage, or child. Currently it fires mid-life on established characters and reads as false.
improvements.why: Cyrus Marchetti is offered 'There is nothing behind you' at age 36 having already had a child at 27, established a maker's career at 21, and married. The card breaks narrative plausibility and the 'starting from nothing' framing appears so often it loses meaning.

improvements.what: Expand the teacher-cluster epitaph pool from 6 lines to 10-12 lines and add a cluster-level seen-recently check (beyond the 2-ancestor lookback) that tracks the last 6 epitaphs session-wide rather than only the last 2 in the current lineage.
improvements.why: The teacher cluster is reached by a wide variety of paths (became_teacher, gave_it_away, scholar_legacy) and the 6-line pool exhausts within a single focused session. Four variations of 'gave everything she knew' land in the 15-dynasty transcript.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 new card clusters in the adult 28-55 band that are NOT contingent on relationship or vocation status — pure character/ethical moments that can vary the middle years for any life shape. Candidates: a creative-crisis card, a political/civic card, a card about an unexpected medical windfall (contrast with the health scare).
improvements.why: The adult band is the thinnest in terms of structural surprise. Players who have seen the love-work-child-health loop across several lives feel the skeleton of the arc by dynasty 5 even when individual card text differs.

improvements.what: Add onceDyn gating to cb_outcast_return so it fires at most once per dynasty, preventing it from being a formulaic 'make friend in yard, get payback in adulthood' expected beat across every dynasty.
improvements.why: The callback's power comes from surprise. Once a player has seen it twice (D2 Felix, D3 Vesna) they expect it whenever they choose 'Sit beside them' in childhood — which collapses the choice from a genuine moral act into a strategic investment.

verdict: A Life is a well-crafted literary toy that delivers genuine pleasure for the first 3-4 dynasties, but the adult structural cadence becomes legible by dynasty 5-6, a handful of verbal phrases repeat visibly enough to break immersion, and the love-and-family arc is close to mechanical by mid-session — leaving it a solid 6.5 rather than the 8 its writing quality otherwise deserves.
